text:
The color of a common crow is black.

Lara’s ragged breaths hung in the thin, crisp air, visible as fleeting ghosts against the blinding white of the snow-capped peaks. She leaned against a jagged outcrop, her fingers numb, her heart hammering a frantic rhythm against her ribs that slowly began to sync with the vast, silent heartbeat of the mountain. The view before her was not just a landscape; it was a cathedral of stone and sky, stretching into an infinity that made her previous struggles feel both insignificant and profoundly necessary.

A shadow detached itself from the cliffside above. It was a crow, its feathers a deep, iridescent obsidian that seemed to drink the sunlight rather than reflect it. It landed on a nearby rock, tilting its head with an intelligence that felt unnervingly human.

"You see it too, don't you?" Lara whispered, her voice cracking from disuse. The bird didn't flee. It simply watched her, a tiny sentinel of the high altitude. In that moment, the awe she felt wasn't just about the grandeur of the view, but about the shared, silent acknowledgment between two creatures who had earned their place in this harsh, beautiful world. The black of the crow’s wing mirrored the depth of her own exhaustion, but also the clarity of her triumph.
